newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault denies discussing Mack sale with Volvo.
newsitem.headline: Renault denies discussing Mack sale with Volvo.

text.p: Renault's trucks unit, Renault V.I., denied a report on Tuesday it was discussing the sale of its U.S.-based Mack Trucks business to Volvo Trucks.
"Renault formally denies that there are any discussions on the sale of Mack," a spokesman for Renault V.I. told Reuters. He said there were no discussions on a cooperation or merger.

The Swedish newspaper Svenska Dagbladet reported Volvo Trucks was planning to buy Mack to double its U.S. market share. It said the sticking point was that Renault would not sell Mack separately. A buyer would have to take the European truck operation as well.

The newspaper said Volvo Trucks officials became familiar with Mack during the preparations in the early 1990s for a planned alliance between Renault and Volvo that ended in failure. It also said Volvo's North American chief executive, Marc Gustafson, was recruited from Mack.
A Volvo Trucks official told Reuters on Tuesday the group was not planning any cooperation other than the discussions being held with Mitsubishi.
